sources.title: Koskenniemi, Kimmo (1981). Syntactic Methods in the Study of the Indus Script.
sources.locator: Printed pp. 125–136; especially pp. 126–128.
sources.scope: Full-text passages inspected: joint segmentation/syntactic analysis and pairwise constraints precede our structural work.

sources.title: Rao et al. (2009). A Markov model of the Indus script.
sources.locator: Main text methods, pp. 5–6; missing-sign section and supplement.
sources.scope: Full-text passages inspected: missing-sign prediction, modified Kneser–Ney and working-corpus deduplication are prior methods.

sources.title: Yadav et al. (2010). Statistical Analysis of the Indus Script Using n-Grams.
sources.locator: Methods and structural/positional results.
sources.scope: Full-text page inspected: n-gram constraints and recurring combinations precede broad structural novelty claims.

sources.title: Bhaskar, M. V. (2024; accepted 2023). Markers and agencies of anisotropy in the Indus sign system.
sources.type: Indian Journal of History of Science article
sources.scope: Full-text passage inspected: physical line division and reading order already form an explicit analytical question. Citation establishes precedent, not agreement with its interpretations.

sources.title: Khanna, Ruhan and Louie Merriam (2025). A Computational Analysis of the Indus Script: Identifying Sign Functions in Logo-Syllabic Writing Systems.
sources.type: International Journal of Computer Applications 187(64) article
sources.locator: pp. 19–22; abstract, introduction and methods.
sources.scope: Full-text passages inspected: distributional sign and pair classification. Proposed semantic classes are hypotheses.

sources.title: Bourdeau, Daniel (2026). The Indus script: Parpola’s decipherment and 2,727 registered tests.
sources.type: public project page and code; unreviewed
sources.locator: Sections 3, 7, 9 and 10 in historical HTML.
sources.scope: Historical file fetched through GitHub connector. Recorded commit date 2026-10-01T20:52:04Z; blob b786b60dc3389bcc0297c23de3b2b8002e9d3b14. Establishes a public overlapping approach before our later packages; no full replication of its results.

sources.title: Parpola, Asko (2008). Is the Indus script indeed not a writing system?
sources.locator: Printed pp. 111–131; proper names and occupation discussion near p. 113.
sources.scope: Full-text passages inspected. Names, occupations and recurring order are prior hypotheses.

sources.title: Mukhopadhyay, Bahata Ansumali (2023). Semantic scope of Indus inscriptions comprising taxation, trade and craft licensing, commodity control and access control: archaeological and script-internal evidence.
sources.type: Humanities and Social Sciences Communications 10:972 article
sources.locator: Abstract, Materials and methods, and structural summary.
sources.scope: Full-text passages inspected. Administrative functions, distant identical texts, and corpus/image reconciliation precede broad claims of novelty. Its semantic conclusions are not adopted as established facts.

sources.title: Kenoyer, J. Mark and Richard H. Meadow (2010). Inscribed Objects from Harappa Excavations 1986–2007.
sources.locator: Accessible manuscript pp. 7–10; seal carving and chronological change.
sources.scope: Full-text passages inspected. Documents changes and late rectangular seals. Does not itself validate our export's mapping of every Vats stratum to HARP subperiods.

sources.title: Fuls, Andreas (2023). The Interactive Corpus of Indus Texts (ICIT) as an epigraphical database and online tool for Indus script research.
sources.locator: Abstract 76.
sources.scope: Abstract inspected: integrated artifact metadata, images and text analysis already exist in ICIT. No independent audit of the full database.

sources.title: Wells and Fuls. Interactive Corpus of Indus Texts.
sources.locator: Indus writing project description.
sources.scope: Project page inspected as provenance and tool precedent; no claim to have queried its full online corpus.

sources.title: Raghavendra, Nikhil (2026). On the Non-Specificity of Statistical Measures Used in Script Decipherment.
sources.locator: Sections 5–7; appendix B unicity arithmetic; appendix C source constraints and lexical reconstruction.
sources.scope: Full-text passages inspected: structured non-language controls, dictionary stress tests, grouped evaluation and unicity counterexample precede our general calibration argument. Our narrower comparison evaluates the complete released key on real Indus inscriptions.

sources.title: Ugrashravas. Panini Protocol.
sources.locator: Home, short-word and US Constitution demonstration descriptions.
sources.scope: Page inspected. Prior criticism and a constructive demonstration, not used as a validated quantitative benchmark. Exact first-release date not pinned here.

sources.title: Winkler et al. (2015). Multi-level block permutation.
sources.locator: Abstract and publication record; doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2015.05.092.
sources.scope: Abstract-level check in this review; PMC and institutional full-text routes were blocked. Established dependence-preserving permutation precedent.

sources.title: Hemerik, Jesse and Jelle Goeman (2018; online 2017). Exact testing with random permutations.
sources.locator: Abstract and conditional Monte Carlo development.
sources.scope: Full-text page inspected. Exact conditional/random-permutation foundations predate our applied examples.

sources.title: Knight, Nair, Rathod and Yamada (2006). Unsupervised Analysis for Decipherment Problems.
sources.locator: Paper introduction and decipherment methods.
sources.scope: Full-text inspected at selected passages; model-based unsupervised decipherment and failure analysis are prior approaches.

sources.title: Luo, Cao and Barzilay (2019). Neural Decipherment via Minimum-Cost Flow: From Ugaritic to Linear B.
sources.locator: Publication page and abstract.
sources.scope: Abstract-level check: constrained matching and known-script evaluations are prior methods. Full algorithm was not independently reimplemented.

sources.title: Allman, Matias and Rhodes (2009). Identifiability of parameters in latent structure models with many observed variables.
sources.locator: Abstract; foundational result also cited in existing project manuscript.
sources.scope: Abstract-level check here; does not constitute an independent proof audit. Generic latent-mixture identifiability is established prior theory.

sources.title: Parpola, Asko (2009). ‘Hind Leg’ + ‘Fish’: Towards Further Understanding of the Indus Script.
sources.locator: Abstract, printed pp. 39–41 and fish/rebus discussions.
sources.scope: Full-text passages inspected: fish compounds and recurring cross-site sequences are prior observations and interpretations.

sources.title: Parpola (1994), Deciphering the Indus Script; Wells (2015), The Archaeology and Epigraphy of Indus Writing.
sources.locator: Wells publisher sample and bibliographic references; Parpola later author summaries.
sources.scope: Full books not exhaustively accessible/checked. Fine-grained priority remains unresolved where these are the nearest potential source.
